network_thesis.headline: One app. Every island run. The water layer of the LINE super-app.
network_thesis.body: LINE is the dominant messaging, payments and on-demand app across Japan, Taiwan and Thailand (as LINE MAN) — three of the world's richest island-leisure travel markets, every one of them still moving on slow conventional ferries. The same in-app foiling tier extends across all three: pick one market to prove it, or roll the recommended sequence. The fleet, the app integration and the captain-partner model are identical everywhere.
network_thesis.how_to_read: Each market is a real, ready launch. Start with Japan — LINE's home market — or pick any market. The phased sequence is our recommended path, not the only one.

partner_context.their_ambition: Extend LINE from messaging + payments + delivery into new high-margin on-demand premium tiers across its three core markets.
partner_context.their_pressure: Mobility and delivery margins are thin against road-network saturation; growth needs modes the car/scooter layer can't reach.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier adds the unmonetised water-leisure tier — a software-defined foiling fleet booking inside the LINE app and LINE Pay wallet.

hero.title: LINE × Navier — the in-app foiling water tier for Japan, Taiwan & Thailand
hero.subtitle: The water layer of the super-app, across three of the world's richest island-leisure markets.
hero.what_we_do_together: A LINE-branded foiling water tier on the busiest island-leisure corridors across Japan, Taiwan and Thailand — booked in LINE, paid in LINE Pay, all-electric and zero-wake.

why_now: LINE owns the messaging, payments and on-demand relationship across Japan, Taiwan and Thailand — three of the world's richest island-leisure travel markets, every one still served by slow conventional ferries. A premium in-app foiling tier is the natural next high-margin layer.

why_navier_now.step_change: A smooth flying crossing instead of a slow, rough conventional ferry on the region's signature island runs.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Existing licensed ferry piers across all three markets serve the routes — Pioneer II needs only a berth.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Dominant super-app penetration + iconic island-leisure demand + an incumbent ferry fleet ripe for a premium upgrade.

multimodal_fit: The same LINE app and LINE Pay wallet that already power LINE Taxi (Japan/Taiwan) and LINE MAN (Thailand) extend to a captain-partner water leg, booking door-to-door with a road leg at each pier.

differentiation.headline: Why Navier, why an in-app water tier
points: A software-defined foiling platform: all-electric, zero-wake, smooth even in chop.
An identical fleet, integration spec and captain-partner model across all three markets.
A live proof network in the Maldives ($100M, ~100 vessels) de-risks the model.

proof_points.claim: LINE is the demand-and-wallet rail across all three markets.
proof_points.evidence: LINE has ~98M monthly active users in Japan (~80% of the population) and ~193M globally; parent LY Corporation (LINE + Yahoo Japan) is one of Japan's largest tech companies. That installed base and LINE Pay are exactly what a premium in-app water tier plugs into.
proof_points.source: LY Corporation Integrated Report FY2024 (MAU as of late March 2025)

proof_points.claim: LINE already runs a billion-dollar on-demand business in the region.
proof_points.evidence: LINE MAN Wongnai — LINE's Thailand super-app — grew 2024 revenue ~17% to ~US$451M (gross profit +35%), serves 10M+ users, is valued above US$1B as Thailand's largest tech unicorn, and reached profitability ahead of a planned 2027 IPO.

proof_points.claim: Clean-fleet policy is turning diesel ferries into stranded assets in LINE's markets.
proof_points.evidence: Japan is committed to carbon neutrality by 2050, with MLIT's 'Roadmap to Zero Emission from Shipping' targeting a first zero-emission ship by 2028; Thailand targets carbon neutrality by 2050 (net-zero by 2065). An all-electric, zero-wake foiling fleet is on the right side of both.
proof_points.source: MLIT Japan; Thailand national climate plan / NDC, 2024–2025

proof_points.claim: The Setouchi art-island corridor already moves world-scale leisure volume on slow ferries.
proof_points.evidence: The Setouchi Triennale art festival drew ~1.17M visitors at its peak (2019), roughly a quarter from overseas — all reaching Naoshima/Teshima on conventional seasonal ferries. A premium in-app foiling hop is the obvious upgrade.

objections.response: Every corridor sits well inside the Pioneer II 70 nm all-electric envelope: Setouchi art islands ~7 nm, Tokyo Bay ~2 nm, Kaohsiung–Donggang ~12 nm, the Penghu mesh ~3–18 nm, Krabi–Phi Phi ~8 nm and Samui–Phangan ~10 nm. No long-range hybrid or charging infrastructure is required.

objections.objection: What about sea state, typhoons and monsoon?
objections.response: Foils lift the hull clear of the surface, so the ride stays smooth where displacement ferries pound. Economics assume calm-season utilisation that aligns with peak leisure demand; the Andaman and Gulf seasons are offset, so a Thai fleet can flex between coasts across the year.

objections.objection: Safety and certification across three jurisdictions?
objections.response: Navier brings software-defined controls, a clear first-of-class certification path, and an operating record across the US and now the Maldives. Pilots stage from existing licensed ferry piers, and the all-electric, zero-wake profile aligns with the strict harbour rules tightening across Japan, Taiwan and Thailand.

objections.objection: Conventional ferries are cheap and frequent.
objections.response: This is a premium in-app tier — faster, far smoother, zero-wake and on demand — additive to, not a price war with, the existing scheduled fleet, and monetising demand the road and ferry layers can't capture.

end_state.headline: The water layer of the super-app — across Japan, Taiwan and Thailand, at scale.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every island-leisure coast LINE serves across its three core markets — Japan (the Setouchi art islands and Tokyo/Yokohama Bay), Taiwan (Kaohsiung and the Penghu chain) and Thailand (the Andaman and Gulf islands, as LINE MAN) — wherever water separates demand from destination.

steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II all-electric across the island hops
steady_state.tam_framing: Three of the world's richest island-leisure travel markets still move on slow, weather-exposed conventional ferries — a multi-billion-dollar premium-mobility surface no super-app has monetised.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is not a pilot count — it is the whole island-leisure map across LINE's three markets. Japan proves the in-app foiling tier in LINE's home market, Thailand scales it on the busiest island-leisure water on earth as LINE MAN, and Taiwan rounds out the mesh. At maturity that is 260+ vessels on 40+ corridors across Japan, Taiwan and Thailand — booked entirely inside the app the region already lives in. The Maldives' ~100-vessel network is the unit; this is that unit replicated across three of Asia's richest leisure coasts (addressable ceiling ~1,030).

growth_case.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
growth_case.modal_headline: Floor to prize — every rung traces to grounded demand

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.headline: Lens shift: Navier captured share → total inducible marine-transfer wallet
ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marine transfer → total journey wallet (food, stays, experiences, in-app ads)
ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.

ladder_transitions.headline: Line platform take on Navier-carried journeys
ladder_transitions.basis: Platform-take step. Platform commission applied to the journey GMV routed through the Navier network (Navier-captured subset, not the full induced market).
ladder_transitions._lb_ref: LB-113: partner_platform_rev_on_navier = on-Navier subset, distinct from deck's '18% × full Journey GMV' narrative ceiling
